qt: to the Commission Majdouline Sbai (Verts/ALE), Tineke Strik (Verts/ALE), Thomas Waitz (Verts/ALE), Sara Matthieu (Verts/ALE), Ana Miranda Paz (Verts/ALE) Subject:

On 25 September 2026, we sent a letter to Commission Executive Vice-President for Prosperity and Industrial Strategy Stéphane Séjourné requesting that the EU’s ‘Strategic project’ label not be awarded to any projects in Bosnia and Herzegovina in the upcoming release of strategic projects. We highlighted that the current Bosnian context of mining and legislative framework do not allow for the fulfilment of the criteria set out in the Critical Raw Materials Act1 (CRMA) for awarding the label. We have not yet received an answer from the Commission, and the release of strategic projects outside of the EU could happen any day now. Therefore, we would like to ask the following: 1.
Is the Commission anticipating the inclusion of any strategic project in Bosnia and Herzegovina in its release for third countries planned for October 2026?

If there were to be any such project, how can the Commission demonstrate that they will respect the criteria set out in the CRMA, and would the environmental part of the evaluation of the project finally be made accessible to the MEPs?

How does the Commission address the anti-EU feeling arising in Bosnia and Herzegovina due to the perception of double standards between the country and the EU when it comes to protecting the environment?

Regulation (EU) 2024/1252 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 establishing a framework for ensuring a secure and sustainable supply of critical raw materials and amending Regulations (EU) No 168/2013, (EU) 2018/858, (EU) 2018/1724 and (EU) 2019/1020 (OJ L, 2024/1252, 3.5.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1252/oj).
